beyond: further away than, or outside the limits of, something
The hiking trail continues far beyond the edge of the forest.
individual: a single person or thing, considered separately
Each individual is responsible for following the safety rules.
homes: The storm damaged dozens of homes along the coast.
city: The old city centre is filled with narrow cobblestone streets.
centres: plural of centre; main locations of an activity or organization
Community centres offer free classes for job seekers every week.
built: constructed, past tense and participle of build
The bridge was built over a hundred years ago and still stands today.
idea: a thought or plan about what to do
She had a brilliant idea for the school fundraiser.
thousands: a very large number of people or things, counted in units of a thousand
Thousands of workers gathered outside the factory to demand better pay.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
morning: the early part of the day, from sunrise until noon
She likes to go jogging in the cool morning air before work.
fewer: Fewer people are buying newspapers than a decade ago.
cafes: plural of cafe; small restaurants serving light meals and drinks
The old town is full of small cafes with outdoor seating.
sandwich: two slices of bread with filling between them
She packed a cheese sandwich for lunch.
shops: places where goods are sold to the public
Small shops line the narrow streets of the old town.
depend: to be affected by or determined by something
Your success in this course will depend on regular practice.
lose: to no longer have something; to be deprived of
If you lose your password, you can reset it online.
customers: people who buy goods or services from a business
The café attracts customers with its freshly roasted coffee.
buildings: structures with walls and a roof, such as houses or offices
Several tall buildings now line the once-quiet waterfront district.
stand: to be in an upright position on one's feet
Please stand near the door until your name is called.
half: one of two equal parts of something
She gave half of the sandwich to her brother.
empty: The bus was almost empty at that late hour.
meanwhile: at the same time, or during the intervening period
Meanwhile, the rest of the team continued preparing for the launch.
residential: relating to areas where people live
New shops have opened in the quiet residential neighbourhood.
neighbourhoods: districts or areas within towns or cities
Wealthier neighbourhoods often have more shade trees than poorer ones.
business: a particular task, activity, or matter to be dealt with
Organizing the wedding turned into a stressful business for everyone involved.
local: relating to a particular, nearby area
The local council approved plans for a new park.
vietnam: Vietnam is known for its long coastline and rich cuisine.
southeast: the direction or region midway between south and east
They spent a month backpacking around Southeast Asia.
asia: the largest continent, covering much of the eastern hemisphere
The company plans to expand its business across Southeast Asia next year.
picture: an image, painting, drawing, or photograph
He hung a picture of the mountains above his desk.
looks: appears to be, has a certain appearance
The sky looks heavy with rain this afternoon.
somewhat: to a moderate degree; a little
The results were somewhat surprising to the research team.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
generations: groups of people born and living at about the same time
The recipe has been passed down through generations.
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
hard: difficult; not easy, or solid to the touch
It was hard to concentrate with all that noise outside.
find: I finally found my keys under the sofa.
internet: the global network connecting computers for communication and information
Slow internet made it difficult for her to join the video call.
connections: links or relationships between two or more things
The new railway created faster connections between the north and south.
vary: to be different or change according to circumstances
Opinions on the new policy vary widely among residents.
hot: The soup was too hot to eat right away.
weather: the state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes the weather it sits in.
air-conditioned: cooled by a machine that controls air temperature
They spent the hottest hours inside an air-conditioned mall.
comfort: a state of physical ease and freedom from pain or stress
The soft blankets offered great comfort during the cold night.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
share: a part of a larger amount that is divided among people
Each partner receives an equal share of the profits.
factories: buildings where goods are manufactured in large quantities
Many factories in the region closed during the recession.
markets: places or systems where goods, services, or assets are traded
Global markets reacted quickly to the news of rising interest rates.
services: systems that supply the public with something needed
Public services such as healthcare rely on tax revenue.
must: used to show that something is necessary or certain
You must show identification before entering the building.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
result: something that happens because of an action or event
The delay was a direct result of the heavy storm.
here: in, at, or to this place
Please leave your bags here by the door.
remained: continued to exist or stayed in the same state
The old bridge remained standing long after the flood destroyed everything else.
occasional: happening sometimes, but not often or regularly
An occasional storm is the only break from the dry season.
arrangement: a plan or agreement made in advance
They reached an arrangement to share the cost of repairs equally.
normal: usual, typical, or expected; not unusual
It is normal to feel nervous before a big exam.
too: The height of the band carries information too.
early: before the usual or expected time
She always arrives early for important meetings.
story: an account of events, real or imagined, told for interest
She wrote a short story about her grandmother's village.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
end: the final part or point of something
Save the best joke for the end of your speech.
reinvented: changed something completely to create a new form
The singer reinvented her style completely for her latest album.
turning: moving or rotating in a circular direction
An effect anyone can feel by holding a turning wheel by its axle.
old: having lived or existed for a long time; not new or young
The old bridge was replaced after decades of heavy use.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
flats: apartments; sets of rooms for living in, on one floor of a building
Many young families rent flats in the city centre.
warehouses: large buildings used for storing goods
Cities turned old factories and warehouses into flats and galleries.
galleries: rooms or buildings where art is displayed
The city is famous for its many small art galleries.
seems: gives the impression of being something
It seems likely that prices will keep rising this year.
certain: Certain foods can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề
Nobody could answer the teacher's difficult question about gravity.
query
inquiry
issue
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
happen: Nobody expected the delay to happen so close to the deadline.
should: used to say what is correct, expected, or advisable
You should see a doctor if the pain continues for another week.
gets: She gets nervous before every public speech.
decide: make a choice or judgment after considering options
The committee will decide next week whether to approve the funding.
